Extract data from full texts with an LLM

Source: R/extraction.R
df_extract_batch.Rd

Sends each full text with the project's extraction prompt and asks for a structured result following _extraction_schema.yml. The result is validated against the schema (including the _ref links between data points and metadata) and cached with its provenance and any validation problems. Use df_import_batch() to move the results into the project.

Usage

df_extract_batch(
  chat,
  files,
  metawoRld_path = ".",
  mode = c("sequential", "parallel", "batch"),
  force = FALSE,
  max_active = 3,
  batch_file = NULL,
  wait = TRUE
)

df_extract(chat, identifier, file, metawoRld_path = ".", ...)

Arguments

chat

An ellmer chat object or "provider/model" string. Use a model that accepts PDFs if you pass PDFs.

files

Named character vector of file paths, names being the study identifiers; or a single folder, in which case files named after the identifiers are used (see df_find_fulltexts()).

metawoRld_path

Project root.

mode

"sequential" (default), "parallel" or "batch" (see df_assess_batch()). Full texts are large, so mind your provider's rate limits when using "parallel".

force

Re-extract even if a current cached result exists.

max_active, batch_file, wait

See df_assess_batch().

identifier

A single study identifier.

file

Path to its full text.

...

Further arguments passed to df_extract_batch().

Value

A tibble with identifier, status ("extracted", "cached", "failed" or "pending"), n_data_points, n_problems (schema validation problems), error, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost.

df_extract(): the extracted data as a list (metadata, data_points), or an error.

Details

Full texts can be PDF (sent as a document to models that support it), plain text/Markdown, or HTML/XML (e.g. JATS from PubMed Central), whose text is extracted first.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic()
todo <- df_pending_extraction("my_review")
# PDFs saved as fulltext/<identifier>.pdf (DOIs with "/" replaced, see df_find_fulltexts())
res <- df_extract_batch(chat, "my_review/fulltext", "my_review")
df_import_batch(metawoRld_path = "my_review")
} # }
